newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent tumbles as Iraq agrees oil sale conditio.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent tumbles as Iraq agrees oil sale conditio.

text.p: IPE Brent futures fell sharply in mid-afternoon trade on news that Baghdad has agreed to all conditions for the U.N./Iraq oil for food deal.
Jan Brent shed earlier gains and moved rapidly into the red to trade 33 cents down at $22.70 a barrel by 1532 GMT.
Iraqi U.N. ambassador Nizar Hamdoon said on Monday that Baghdad has agreed to all U.N. conditions that had held up the implementation of the deal.
First Iraqi oil could start flowing some time in December, Hamdoon predicted.
"The market is bound to fall on this type of news, but it is still focused on winter and heating oil demand," said Alistair Harris of brokers MeesPierson Derivatives in London.
He pegged support for Jan Brent around $22.60-$22.65 a barrel.
The oil for food deal will allow Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicines.
Dec gas oil was trading $3.75 a tonne lower at $219 by 1537 GMT.
Hamdoon also said that a pipeline leading from northern Iraq to Turkey, through which the bulk of the oil is due to pass, "will definitely be ready by the first week of December."
He said the final obstacle was the approval of the pricing formula which he said should be obtained this week.
Brokers also had an eye on the OPEC meeting in Vienna. Most were expecting a rollover of the cartel's 25.03 million barrels per day production ceiling.
